title: Manager - Legal Counsel
description:
**About the Opportunity**
=========================

Job Type: PermanentApplication Deadline: 22 October 2026

**Job Description**

**Title** **Manager - Legal Counsel**

**Department** **Legal**

**Location****Gurgaon**

**Reports To****Senior Legal Counsel**

**Level** **5**

We’re proud to have been helping our clients build better financial futures for over 50 years. How have we achieved this? By working together - and supporting each other - all over the world. So, join our team and feel like you’re part of something bigger.

**About your team**

You will be part of the India Legal Team, within the Commercial Legal vertical, front-ending drafting, review and negotiation of procurement and commercial contracts supporting Fidelity International's internal business units (Technology, HR, CPS, Marketing, Finance, etc.) and sourcing functions across global offices.

As part of Fidelity’s General Counsel function (Group Legal and Tax ), you will work closely with our legal, tax, regulatory compliance and commercial counterparts based in the Asia Pacific, United Kingdom, Continental Europe, Canada and other jurisdictions on cross border support covering commercial contracts, business legal document, Company Secretariat and other legal documentation.

The team’s focus is on providing agile, pragmatic, business-aligned legal support while minimizing reliance on external counsel and ensuring minimum legal / regulatory exposure to the organisation.

**About your role**

This is a fast-paced role within the Commercial Legal team, requiring high-quality legal analysis, risk assessment, and cross-border engagement. You will need a strong sense of commercial understanding, attention to detail, adaptability, and the ability to work at pace with confidence.

Key aspects of your role include:

  

* Providing front-end legal support for drafting, reviewing, and negotiating a wide range of procurement and commercial agreements, with particular emphasis on emerging technologies such as cloud services and GenAI.

  

* Interfacing directly with global stakeholders and advising on legal and compliance issues linked to onboarding third-party tech solutions or developing in-house capabilities, including those involving staff augmentation and temporary workforce arrangements.
* Collaborating with colleagues across functions and geographies to deliver pragmatic, business-aligned legal solutions.

Contributing to continuous process improvement, knowledge sharing, and technology adoption within the team.

We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of background, and strive to create an environment where everyone can thrive.

**Key Responsibilities**

  

* Draft, review and negotiate a variety of procurement and commercial contracts, including both technology and non-technology engagements such as Cloud Outsourcing Agreements, SaaS, IaaS, Software Licences, Master Services Agreements, Statements of Work, Consulting and Facilities Agreements, Change Orders, and Data Processing Agreements.
* Advise business and sourcing teams on onboarding RFPs, third-party AI and GenAI solutions or developing these in-house, including IP, data, ethics, and regulatory considerations.
* Understand and interpret international Tech/Cloud Outsourcing regulations (ESMA, EBA, EIOPA, etc.) and apply them to contracts.
* Support contracts related to staff augmentation, consulting, professional services, and temporary staffing models across geographies and understanding of local regulatory nuances e.g., TUPE, Principal Employer responsibilities.
* Collaborate with procurement to resolve legal and commercial issues and maintain compliance with company policies.
* Provide legal advice on matters related to existing procurement contracts and ongoing supplier service engagements.
* Provide support in managing commercial disputes and arbitration matters, including coordination with external counsel when required.
* Coach and guide junior legal team members.
* May represent legal function / lead project teams as required.
* Contribute to continuous process improvement, knowledge sharing, and technology adoption within the team.
* Demonstrate adaptability, collaboration, and a proactive approach in all interactions.

**About you**

In this role you will be required to have:

  

* LLB with 7-9 years of post-qualification experience, preferably in an in-house role within a multinational organisation (Financial Services, Asset Management, or Information Technology industries preferred).
* Solid experience in high complexity procurement and commercial contracts, covering both technology and non-technology engagements, including cloud services (SaaS, IaaS), outsourcing, software licensing, market data, consulting, facilities, and staff augmentation.
* Experience in handling commercial disputes and arbitration matters, with an understanding of dispute resolution strategy and contract enforcement.
* Working knowledge of global cloud outsourcing regulatory frameworks (e.g., ESMA, EBA, DORA, PRA, MAS) and their application to tech contracts.
* Familiarity with current technology trends such as AI, GenAI, platform integration, data processing, and their legal and regulatory implications.
* Strong oral and written communication skills; excellent judgment; business sense.
* Excellent drafting and negotiation skills.
* Commercial judgement, business acumen, pragmatic and a solutions-oriented mindset.
* High ethical standards and professional integrity.
* Strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple matters in parallel.
* Experience working on cross-border contracts and international engagements.
* Self-motivated team player with a willingness to learn and adopt legal tech tools (e.g., Harvey, ChatGPT).
* Experience with contract management systems, e-signature platforms, and other legal technology tools is desirable.
* Demonstrated adaptability, collaboration, and a proactive approach.
* Positive, pro-active attitude suited to be a team member within a dynamic business environment.
* Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to instil confidence and to build strong relationships with stakeholders.

**Feel rewarded**

For starters, we’ll offer you a comprehensive benefits package. We’ll value your wellbeing and support your development. And we’ll be as flexible as we can about where and when you work – finding a balance that works for all of us. It’s all part of our commitment to making you feel motivated by the work you do and happy to be part of our team. For more about our work, our approach to dynamic working and how you could build your future here, visit careers.fidelityinternational.com.

For more about our work, our approach to dynamic working and how you could build your future here, visit careers.fidelityinternational.com.

title: Senior Legal Counsel
description:
**Senior Legal Counsel, Transformation & Service Enablement**
-------------------------------------------------------------

**Field**

Location- Gurgaon, India

Reports to- Head of Legal, Risk & Compliance Shared Services

Department- Legal, Risk & Compliance Shared Services Hub

### **Role Description**

The Senior Legal Counsel, Transformation & Service Enablement leads the design, transition and continuous improvement of legal services within FNZ’s India Legal, Risk & Compliance Shared Services Hub. The role is accountable for mobilizing new services, programme and project delivery, process and control design, SOPs and knowledge enablement, data-led improvement, and the development of AI, automation and legal-technology use cases within agreed governance. The role combines credible legal judgement with strong transformation, legal-operations, programme-delivery and change-management capability. It does not own platforms, governance or substantive legal positions assigned to Legal Operations, Procurement, Technology or onshore legal teams, and it partners with the Service Delivery & Workforce leader to transfer stabilized services into business-as-usual operations.

### **Team Responsibilities**

* Lead the Hub transition, transformation and service-enablement portfolio.
* Design and mobilize scalable services, processes, controls, documentation and hand-offs.
* Drive responsible AI, workflow automation, self-service and contract-process optimization within owner governance.
* Coordinate Hub knowledge, templates, playbooks, SOPs and change-adoption activity while preserving substantive ownership.
* Use operational data to prioritize improvement and demonstrate benefits.

### **Specific Role Responsibilities**

**1. Transition and Mobilization**

* Own transition plans, workstream governance, milestones, risks, dependencies and stakeholder communications for new services entering the Hub.
* Lead discovery, scope confirmation, process mapping, knowledge transfer, training packs, readiness assessment, hyper care and stabilization.
* Define entry, exit and BAU acceptance criteria with the Service Delivery & Workforce leader and relevant onshore owner.
* Conduct post-transition reviews and apply lessons learned to future mobilizations.
* Maintain a transition pipeline aligned to the phased service catalogue and avoid mobilizing work whose ownership, risk treatment or prerequisites are unresolved.

**2. Process, Knowledge and Service Design**

* Design fit-for-purpose intake, triage, workflow, escalation, quality and control processes.
* Create and maintain process maps, SOPs, operating documentation, training packs and controlled hand-off materials.
* Coordinate template, precedent, clause-library and playbook administration, version control and implementation using content approved by the relevant onshore legal owner.
* Assess new service requests for feasibility, standardization, automation potential, capability needs and transition readiness.

**3. Legal Technology, AI and Automation**

* Develop and deliver a prioritized portfolio of Hub legal-technology, AI and automation use cases within approved governance.
* Lead workflow automation, self-service, clause automation, abstraction and AI-agent pilots where allocated to the Hub.
* Partner with Legal Operations, Procurement, Technology, Information Security, Privacy and onshore Legal teams on design, controls, testing and deployment.
* Document use cases, assumptions, risks, testing and decisions, with clear human oversight and escalation controls.
* Build adoption plans, user testing, benefits measures and post-implementation reviews with the delivery leader and platform owner.

**4. Continuous Improvement, Data and Change**

* Use operational and stakeholder data to identify bottlenecks, root causes, standardization and redesign opportunities.
* Own the Hub improvement roadmap and project governance, with clear outcomes, owners, dependencies and benefits.
* Coordinate KPI dashboards, trend analysis and management information for improvement purposes, while respecting Legal Operations ownership of ExCo, Board or enterprise reporting where applicable.
* Lead change impact assessment, communications, training, adoption and reinforcement for new processes and tools.
* Develop new Hub service propositions jointly with delivery and onshore owners once legal, operational and technology prerequisites are met.

### **Experience Required**

* A credible legal background, with qualification and PQE appropriate to FNZ’s Senior Legal Counsel architecture.
* Substantial experience leading legal-service transitions, transformation programmers, projects or legal-operations initiatives.
* Demonstrated experience in process design, SOPs, controls, knowledge enablement and organizational change.
* Practical experience developing or implementing legal-technology, AI, workflow automation or self-service use cases.
* Strong programme governance, stakeholder management, risk and dependency management, and benefits-realization experience.
* Experience in financial services, fintech, technology, outsourcing or another regulated environment is desirable.
* Commercial-contracting experience sufficient to understand legal workflows, playbooks, risk thresholds and escalation design.

### **Key Capabilities**

* Transformation leadership and disciplined programme delivery.
* Legal-process design, standardization and control thinking.
* Practical AI, automation and legal-technology enablement.
* Change management, adoption and stakeholder engagement.
* Data-led diagnosis, prioritization and benefits tracking.
* Strong judgement about ownership boundaries, governance and when substantive legal input is required.

*About FNZ*

*FNZ is committed to opening up wealth so that everyone, everywhere can invest in their future on their terms. We know the foundation to do that already exists in the wealth management industry, but complexity holds firms back.*

*We created wealth’s growth platform to help. We provide a global, end-to-end wealth management platform that integrates modern technology with business and investment operations. All in a regulated financial institution.*

*We partner with the world’s leading financial institutions, with over US$2.5 trillion in assets on platform (AoP).*  
  
*Together with our clients, we empower nearly 30 million people across all wealth segments to invest in their future.*

title: Analyst- Compliance & Risk Management
description:
JLL supports the Whole You, personally and professionally.
  
  
Our people at JLL are shaping the future of real estate for a better world by combining world class services, advisory and technology to our clients. We are committed to hiring the best, most talented people in our industry; and we support them through professional growth, flexibility, and personalized benefits to manage life in and outside of work. Whether you’ve got deep experience in commercial real estate, skilled trades, and technology, or you’re looking to apply your relevant experience to a new industry, we empower you to shape a brighter way forward so you can thrive professionally and personally.
  
  
**Analyst AML KYC/Sanctions:**  
Global Legal & Compliance Unit at JBS Gurgaon
  
  
What this job involves
  
  
The AML & KYC / Sanctions Screening Analyst is a role under JLL’s Global Legal Compliance (GLC) team. The KYC / Sanctions Screening Analyst will be located in a JLL Business Services (JBS) shared service centre, and will report to the Compliance / Sanctions Screening Manager within JBS.
  
  
**The KYC / Sanctions Screening Analyst will be responsible for:**
  

* Offering compliant workarounds / alternatives where confronted by obstacles to complete AML KYC;
* Reviewing and resolving false positives from automated daily ongoing screening;
* Manual uploads of names for initial screening in JLL’s global sanctions screening system;
* Extracting data from screening system and forwarding screening results to relevant parties within JLL;
* Escalating potential true matches to appropriate parties within JLL, according to sanctions screening escalation procedures, for further investigation and resolution;
* Ensuring screening procedures are followed consistently with a documented audit trail for all KYC / sanction match resolution actions taken;
* Reviewing preliminary KYC / AML materials liaising with relevant business and local legal & compliance counterparties in line with JLL’s minimum global standards

**Sound like you? To apply you need to be:** –
  
  
The KYC / Sanctions Screening Analyst must have a good knowledge and understanding of sanction law requirements, AML Regulations and KYC best practices, in addition to good technical skills to be able to navigate JLL’s sanctions screening system, extract data from the system and forward to others for escalation and resolution procedures. This includes proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and Adobe PDF. The Analyst must also be able to efficiently identify false matches and conduct initial investigation into potential true matches, and must have good communication and organizational skills to work with local Legal & Compliance teams and continuously follow up on open cases through proper resolution of potential matches identified in the system.
  
  
The AML checks to be conducted on Clients and counterparties which will include: (i) listed companies (and their subsidiaries), (ii) regulated companies (and their subsidiaries), (iii) private individuals and families, (iv) trusts, foundations and unincorporated associated, (v) governments and public authorities, (vi) private and unlisted companies (including special purpose vehicles).
  
An ability to navigate JLL’s Customer Relationship Management (e.g. Salesforce, MS Dynamics) and AML KYC systems (e.g. World Check, Bureau Van Dyke), extract data from the system and forward to others for escalation and resolution procedures is important. This includes proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and Adobe PDF.
  
The Analyst must also be able to identify false matches efficiently and conduct initial investigation into potential true matches of PEPs / Sanctions / Negative, and must have good communication and organisational skills to work with the EMEA AML Team and continuously follow up through to conclusion any open AML KYC checks
  
  
Key skills
  
  

* Prior experience with a large multinational financial institution in respect of sanctions screening and AML/KYC Checks, as well as familiarity with the US OFAC and other international sanctions laws is essential.
* Candidate needs to have some India specific AML experience, as well as familiarity with the other international sanctions laws is essential.
* Minimum 1 years’ experience with Global sanctions screening, Anti-Money Laundering, Know Your Client checks or compliance related field, and with a large multinational financial institution or similar.

Employee specification
  
  

* 2-year Associate’s Degree or equivalent.
* Strong understanding of OFAC and other international sanctions laws and Money Laundering Regulations.
* Good technical skills – proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook, and Adobe PDF and online research tools.
* Team player and self-starter with ability to work proactively and co-operatively with others.
* Excellent communications and problem-solving skills.
* Fluent English language skills essential – further language(s) beneficial
* Strong organisation and prioritization skills, to handle and keep track of high volume of records and cases.

**What we can do for you:**  
At JLL, we make sure that you become the best version of yourself by helping you realize your full potential in an entrepreneurial and inclusive work environment. We will empower your ambitions through our dedicated Total Rewards Program, competitive pay and benefits package.
  
  
Apply today!
  
If this job description resonates with you, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all of the requirements below. We’re interested in getting to know you and what you bring to the table!
  
  
Personalized benefits that support personal well-being and growth:
  
  
JLL recognizes the impact that the workplace can have on your wellness, so we offer a supportive culture and comprehensive benefits package that prioritizes mental, physical and emotional health.
  
  
About JLL –
  
  
We’re JLL—a leading professional services and investment management firm specializing in real estate. We have operations in over 80 countries and a workforce of over 102,000 individuals around the world who help real estate owners, occupiers and investors achieve their business ambitions. As a global Fortune 500 company, we also have an inherent responsibility to drive sustainability and corporate social responsibility. That’s why we’re committed to our purpose to shape the future of real estate for a better world. We’re using the most advanced technology to create rewarding opportunities, amazing spaces and sustainable real estate solutions for our clients, our people, and our communities.
  
  
Our core values of teamwork, ethics and excellence are also fundamental to everything we do and we’re honored to be recognized with awards for our success by organizations both globally and locally.
  
  
Creating a diverse and inclusive culture where we all feel welcomed, valued and empowered to achieve our full potential is important to who we are today and where we’re headed in the future. And we know that unique backgrounds, experiences and perspectives help us think bigger, spark innovation and succeed together.

title: Assistant Director-Manager-Data Privacy-Incident Response
description:

**Job description**
-------------------


Requisition ID: 1743966
At EY, you’ll have the chance to build a career as unique as you are, with the global scale, support, inclusive culture and technology to become the best version of you. And we’re counting on your unique voice and perspective to help EY become even better, too. Join us and build an exceptional experience for yourself, and a better working world for all.

  


**Role description**


**Group**: GDS GCO Enablement Team

  


**The opportunity**



This is a fantastic opportunity to be part of a leading firm whilst playing an instrumental role in advising on data privacy related matters. We are looking for an experienced lawyer with expertise in the data privacy domain to join EY’s Global Delivery Services (GDS) team supporting the General Counsel’s Office (GCO).



The successful candidate will work closely with the Global Lead Counsel – Data Incident Response (a Director in Global Data Protection responsible for the Global Incident Response program) to support the maintenance, coordination and continuous improvement of the Global Incident Response (IR) Program in collaboration with key stakeholders and data protection teams around the world.



The role will also play a key part in supporting the management of multijurisdictional incident responses.



You will work closely with business and Information Security stakeholders and Data Protection leadership and team members.

  


**Your key responsibilities**


* Provide legal oversight and guidance on the management of global data protection and privacy incidents ensuring compliance with EY policies, applicable laws, and regulatory requirements.
* Support the Global Deputy Lead Counsel – Data Protection Incident Response and the Chief Privacy Officer in the management of complex and strategically significant data incidents.
* Coordinate with Information Security, Risk Management, General Counsel teams, and other key stakeholders to ensure data incidents are managed consistently and effectively across jurisdictions.
* Develop and maintain oversight of data incident tracking, reporting, metrics, and trend analysis to support risk management and executive reporting across the EY organisation.
* Support the implementation and continuous improvement of EY’s global data incident response framework, policies, procedures, and governance processes.
* Communicate the global data incident response programme and related requirements, providing guidance and support on the management of cross\-border data incidents
* Identify, assess, and escalate significant legal and regulatory issues arising from data incidents, including matters involving complex jurisdictional considerations or emerging regulatory developments.
* Collaborate with various stakeholders, including data protection, risk management, Infosec and General Counsel teams globally to ensure a coordinated response to incidents.
* Contribute to the development and delivery of training, awareness initiatives, and guidance materials to strengthen understanding of data protection obligations and data incident response requirements across EY.
* Oversee onboarding, capability building, and career development initiatives within the team.
* Allocate work, manage utilization, and ensure delivery aligned with SLAs, quality measures, and stakeholder expectations.
* Provide coaching, performance feedback, and development support to team members.
* Stakeholder management and assistance in business development initiatives.

  


**Skills and attributes for success**


* Demonstrated experience managing complex, cross\-border data incidents and advising senior stakeholders on legal, regulatory, and risk considerations.
* Strong knowledge of EU and international data protection laws, particularly the GDPR, with familiarity with privacy legislation in other key jurisdictions considered advantageous.
* Experience interpreting and applying legal requirements relating to personal data breaches, regulatory investigations, law enforcement requests, and crisis management scenarios.
* Excellent legal judgement, analytical skills, and the ability to provide practical, risk\-based advice in high\-pressure situations.
* Strong stakeholder management and communication skills.
* Experience working in a complex global organisation and managing matters across multiple jurisdictions and cultures.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
* Have a good understanding of emerging technologies such as cloud computing, RPA, AI etc.
* Experiences in client handling and leading a team of legal professionals.
* Ability to team effectively with onshore legal team and colleagues in other functions.
* Highly responsive with ability to manage high workload volumes efficiently and effectively
* Solution oriented with focus on exceptional client service.
* Confidence, maturity and high degree of awareness to be able to work effectively with a broad base of senior\-level internal stakeholders.
* Sensitivity to intercultural contacts and communication.
* Strong sense of personal responsibility and ownership for success of a given task.
* Eagerness to contribute to a team\-oriented environment and ability to work cooperatively with other teams and country practices, demonstrating cultural sensitivity;
* Ability to adapt, cross\-skill, up\-skill and work towards continuous improvements to improve efficiencies and processes within the team.

  


**To qualify for the role, you must have**


**Qualifications**


* Must be a qualified lawyer with consistent strong academic record.
* Mandatory a CIPP (E) certified. Other recognised privacy certifications (e.g., CIPM, CIPT) will be considered an advantage.

  


**Experience**


* Minimum 8 years of years of**relevant** post\-qualification experience (preferably in a multi\-national corporate).

  


**Other Personal Characteristics**


* Unquestioned ethics and integrity.
* High level of self\-confidence and energy.
* High level of intellectual agility, self\-motivation, resourcefulness, and patience.
* Attention to detail.

  


**What working at EY offers**



EY Global Delivery Services (GDS) is a dynamic and truly global delivery network. We work across ten countries – Argentina, India, China, Philippines, Poland, Mexico, Spain, UK, Hungary, Sri Lanka – and with teams from all EY service lines, geographies and sectors, playing a vital role in the delivery of the EY growth strategy. From accountants to coders, we offer a wide variety of fulfilling career opportunities that span all business disciplines. In GDS, you will collaborate with EY teams on exciting projects and work with well\-known brands from across the globe. We’ll introduce you to an ever\-expanding ecosystem of people, learning, skills and insights that will stay with you throughout your career.

  


**EY \| Building a better working world**

  

EY exists to build a better working world, helping to create long\-term value for clients, people and society and build trust in the capital markets.

  

Enabled by data and technology, diverse EY teams in over 150 countries provide trust through assurance and help clients grow, transform and operate.

  


Working across assurance, consulting, law, strategy, tax and transactions, EY teams ask better questions to find new answers for the complex issues facing our world today.

title: Company Secretary
description:
Job Title: Company Secretary (CS)  

Location: Gurugram  

Experience: 3\+ years post\-qualification  

Employment Type: Full\-time  

Job Summary  

We are looking for an experienced Company Secretary to independently manage end\-to\-end  

corporate secretarial and statutory compliances. The role requires close interaction with promoters  

and senior management and the ability to set up governance and compliance frameworks in a  

growing organization.  

Key Responsibilities  

* Manage the entire spectrum of corporate secretarial functions in compliance with the Companies


Act, 2013 and other applicable laws  

* Handle company incorporation, restructuring, and post\-incorporation compliances, including


drafting and filing of statutory forms with ROC and MCA  

* Ensure timely filing of annual, event\-based, and regulatory returns and monitor compliance


deadlines  

* Maintain and update statutory registers, records, and secretarial documentation in physical and


electronic form  

* Plan, convene, and manage Board Meetings, Committee Meetings, and General


Meetings,including preparation of agendas, notices, minutes, and resolutions  

* Advise promoters and senior management on corporate governance, compliance


requirements,and regulatory best practices  

* Coordinate with auditors, legal counsels, company law consultants, and regulatory authorities for


compliance\-related matters  

* Support share capital management activities including allotment, transfer, transmission, and


related statutory filings  

* Assist in implementation and monitoring of corporate policies, governance frameworks, and


compliance risk management processes  

* Track regulatory changes and ensure timely implementation of amendments applicable to the


company  

* Provide secretarial support for strategic initiatives such as investments, funding, restructuring,


and corporate actions  

* Ensure accuracy, completeness, and timely maintenance of all statutory and corporate records


Eligibility \& Experience  

* Qualified Company Secretary (ACS mandatory)
* Minimum 3 years of post\-qualification experience
* Strong hands\-on experience in ROC and MCA compliances
* Experience in startups/NBFCs, or fast\-growing organizations preferred
* Sound knowledge of Companies Act, 2013 and corporate governance practices
* Ability to work independently with minimal supervision


Skills \& Competencies  

* Strong drafting, documentation, and analytical skills
* High level of integrity, attention to detail, and accountability
* Effective communication and stakeholder management skills
* Ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic environment


Compensation  

As per industry standards and experience.

**ABOUT US**


At OakNorth, we're on a mission to empower ambitious businesses and the communities they serve. Since 2015, we've lent over $21 billion across the UK and US, helped create more than 58,000 new homes and 36,000 new jobs, and supported hundreds of thousands of personal savers — all while driving economic growth in the markets we serve.


**ABOUT THE TEAM**


The Legal and Governance team provides expert company secretarial and corporate governance support across OakNorth's group entities. Working closely with the UK\-based Company Secretary and Deputy Company Secretary, the team ensures that all legal entities are effectively managed, statutory obligations are met, and the Board and executive management are well supported on governance and compliance matters.


**ABOUT THE ROLE**


We're looking for a Manager, Company Secretary to join our Gurugram team, working alongside the Deputy Company Secretary to deliver high\-quality governance and corporate secretarial support across the group. You'll own board and committee coordination, maintain statutory records, ensure multi\-jurisdictional regulatory compliance, and act as a key liaison between the organisation and its stakeholders. This is a senior, autonomous role suited to a qualified Chartered Secretary with a sharp eye for detail and strong experience in a group or multinational environment.


**WHAT YOU'LL DO**


* Organise, schedule, and prepare agendas for Board and committee meetings; coordinate production of board papers in line with agreed timelines; attend meetings, record accurate minutes, and track follow\-up actions.
* Ensure the Board's compliance with statutory obligations and best practices in corporate governance; assist in developing and implementing governance policies and frameworks.
* Maintain and update the company secretarial database and group structure chart, ensuring timely and accurate information on all group companies is recorded.
* Ensure compliance with relevant corporate laws, regulations, and industry standards across all jurisdictions where the group operates; monitor legislative changes and advise the Board and management on implications.
* Maintain statutory registers and ensure timely filing of annual returns, financial statements, and other required disclosures; draft and oversee execution of legal documents including shareholder agreements, resolutions, and contracts.
* Collaborate with risk management and compliance teams to maintain robust internal controls; establish processes to identify and mitigate governance\-related risks.
* Manage shareholder queries and oversee the organisation of AGMs and other shareholder interactions; facilitate governance and compliance training for Board members and senior management.
* Collate KYC information as required and support the group in managing legal risks, liaising with external counsel where necessary.

**YOU'LL BE A GREAT FIT IF YOU HAVE…**


* Chartered Secretary qualification (ICSA/CGI or equivalent), with a Bachelor's degree in Law, Business, or a related field; advanced degrees preferred.
* 5\+ years of experience in a similar company secretarial role, ideally within a group or multinational organisation.
* Strong knowledge of corporate law, governance practices, and regulatory frameworks, with the ability to work across multiple jurisdictions.
* Excellent organisational, project management, and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with senior stakeholders and handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion.
* Ability to work autonomously to strict deadlines, manage competing priorities under pressure, and take a proactive approach to governance.

**Nice to Have**


* Experience managing compliance across multiple jurisdictions.
* Familiarity with company secretarial software platforms.
* Advanced degree in Law or Business Administration.

**WHAT WE OFFER**


* **Health \& Protection:** Comprehensive medical cover for you, your family, and parents, along with life and accidental insurance cover at a multiple of your salary.
* **Wellbeing:** Annual health check\-ups, online doctor consultations, pharmacy discounts, nutritionist support, and Employee Assistance Program (EAP) services — all sponsored by OakNorth.
* **Time Off:** Earned leave, casual/sick leave, public holidays, maternity leave, and paternity leave.
* **Life Milestones:** Financial support for important life events such as marriage, childbirth, and bereavement.
* **Flexible Benefits:** Tax\-efficient allowances for internet, fuel, meals, leave travel, and National Pension System (NPS) contributions.
* **Growth \& Development:** Support for professional certifications, learning and development opportunities, childcare benefits, and paid volunteering days.
* **Our Workplace:** Modern, centrally located offices, weekly business updates, team events, and great coffee. We work hard to build a culture worth showing up for.

title: Contracts Professional
description:
Location
Gurgaon, All IN Regions, India
Capabilities
Enterprise Functions
Office Setup
Hybrid
Job ID
\#45380
  
Industry
Enterprise Functions
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission\-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting\-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.


Your impact
As a Contracts Professional within the Global Contracting Center (GCC), you will partner closely with the Contract Management Group, Legal, Sales, Business Operations, and Project Delivery teams throughout the contract lifecycle. You will serve as a trusted advisor on contractual matters, supporting commercial objectives while ensuring appropriate risk identification, assessment, and mitigation.


This role requires a commercially focused legal professional with strong contract review, drafting, negotiation, and analytical skills who can independently manage a broad range of client\-facing agreements and support strategic business initiatives.


**Key Responsibilities**


* Review, draft, redline, and negotiate client contracts, amendments, subcontract agreements, task orders, change requests, non\-disclosure agreements, teaming agreements, and other commercial documents.
* Support RFP, RFQ, and tender reviews from a contractual and compliance perspective.
* Prepare contract summaries, representation \& certification memo, risk assessments, and briefing notes for internal reviews and approvals.
* Identify contractual, legal, and commercial risks and propose solutions consistent with company policies and risk profile.
* Support business teams during contract negotiations with customers and project stakeholders.
* Assist Regional Legal Counsel with complex contractual issues and escalations.
Here's what you'll need
* Law Graduate/LL.B., from a recognized university with 5\-7 years of relevant post\-qualification experience in contract review, drafting and negotiation.
* Demonstrated experience supporting preferably seller side contracting for professional services, engineering, consulting, technology, construction, or infrastructure organizations.
* Preferred experience in reviewing and negotiating public sector customer facing commercial agreements.
* Advanced understanding of contract law principles, risk allocation provisions, compliance framework and commercial contracting practices.
* Experience in interpreting RFPs, RFQs, client terms and conditions, and contractual requirements.
* Ability to effectively collaborate with global stakeholders, including legal, contracting, and business teams.
* Experience working with contract lifecycle management platforms (e.g., Icertis, SAP Ariba)
* Experience working in an in\-house legal department, shared services center or environment supporting global stakeholders.
* Demonstrate ability to independently manage a high volume of contract reviews and negotiations with minimal supervision.
* Team player having strong written and verbal English communication skills with the ability to communicate complex contractual concepts clearly and concisely.
* Provide guidance and day\-to\-day support to junior contracting professionals and assist with knowledge sharing and process improvement initiatives within the GCC.
* Strong analytical, organizational, stakeholder management capabilities, ability to manage multiple priorities and work independently.
At Jacobs we value people. Having the right balance of belonging, career and lifestyle enables us to consistently deliver and exceed clients’ expectations.  

  

Working alongside industry leaders, you will have the opportunity to develop your career working on key projects in an environment which encourages collaboration, knowledge sharing and innovation. To support your professional growth, Jacobs flexible working arrangements, extended leave options and a host of social, health and wellbeing events and initiatives will underpin our commitment to you.  

  

At Jacobs it’s all about what you do, not where you are, which counts!  

  

  

We value collaboration and believe that in\-person interactions are crucial for both our culture and client delivery. We empower employees with our hybrid working policy, allowing them to split their work week between Jacobs offices/projects and remote locations enabling them to deliver their best work.

  

  

Your application experience is important to us, and we’re keen to adapt to make every interaction even better. If you require further support or reasonable adjustments with regards to the recruitment process (for example, you require the application form in a different format), please contact the team via Careers Support.
